public_rationale: The October 14, 2026 study links training compute to frontier performance differences among models released in 2022–2025; it does not test whether scaling alone can reach AGI [e1]. OpenAI’s September 3, 2026 disclosure describes pre-training, reinforcement learning and alignment, without isolating the contribution of scale or establishing that additional methods were necessary [e2]. The AGI Society assessment finds the published evidence insufficient to establish that Astra achieved AGI [e3]. These items establish neither AGI through scaling alone nor a conclusive general limitation on that route, leaving the forecast unresolved [e1, e2, e3].
limitations: Benchmark correlations do not establish whether scaling alone is sufficient for AGI [e1].
The disclosure does not isolate scale from other development methods [e2].
The contract leaves the AGI threshold, baseline method and treatment of reinforcement learning and inference-time compute unspecified.
The e3 metadata gives September 14, 2026, while its displayed text gives September 10, 2026.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Scaling alone was never going to be enough to reach AGI.

statement.excerpt: LLMs are not AGI, and (on their own) never will be; scaling alone was never going to be enough.
statement.document_title: August 5, 2024, a big day in tech?

from_speaker: was never going to be enough
our_interpretation: Read the sentence as an unlimited prediction that increasing the scale of LLMs alone cannot reach AGI.
Read AGI as broadly human-level ability to learn, reason and apply knowledge across unfamiliar intellectual tasks.
Read scaling alone as increasing model size, training data and compute while retaining the underlying method, without an essential new algorithm or external reasoning system.
Whether inference-time computation and reinforcement learning count as scaling must be disclosed rather than silently assumed.
'Scaling alone' defines the qualifying development route; it is not a separate contingent antecedent.
criteria.support_condition: A conclusive general result establishes that scaling the specified LLM approach cannot reach AGI. Limited gains, present failures or use of other methods do not prove necessity.
criteria.contradiction_condition: An independently validated AGI system is shown, through technical disclosure and suitable comparisons, to have reached that capability through scaling the existing LLM method alone.

evidence.excerpt: At the frontier, 80–90% of performance differences are explained by higher training compute, implying that scale—not proprietary technology—drives frontier advances.
evidence.explanation: The study provides material evidence that scale explains much observed frontier performance variation. Its analysis of models released during 2022–2025 does not establish that scaling alone reaches AGI.

evidence.excerpt: GPT‑6 Astra brings together years of research and big bets across pre-training, reinforcement learning, and alignment.
evidence.explanation: The company describes several development approaches. This disclosure does not isolate scaling alone, and use of additional approaches does not prove they were necessary.

evidence.excerpt: Our current evaluation is that the published evidence does not yet support concluding that GPT-6 Astra represents the achievement Artificial General Intelligence.
evidence.locator: Opening assessment, before Evidence available for GPT-6 Astra
evidence.explanation: This assessment reviews prominent AGI declarations but finds the public evidence insufficient. It is an assessment of existing evidence, not a proof that scaling cannot reach AGI.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Independent validation of AGI, supported by technical disclosures and controlled comparisons establishing that scaling the existing LLM method alone produced it, would contradict the claim. A conclusive general result establishing that this route cannot reach AGI would support it.
